sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. Organic Recycling Systems is a municipal-waste technology, EPC and waste-to-energy operating group, now also exposed to acquired chemical distribution. It is a project-growth and refinancing special situation, not an established compounder. Repeat projects and the Solapur operating franchise are the strongest evidence for the business; poor cumulative cash realization, an unbridged acquisition and economically large preference claims are the decisive risks. At the qualified 19 October price₹209.55, market capitalization is₹326.88 cr and reported FY26 P/E is 13.03x. That optical multiple ignores the difference between preference par and actual redemption economics. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS rather than imputed scores. No ordinary entry range is supported. Obtain a reliable acquisition/cash/claim bridge and binding funded execution plan before considering price as the main obstacle.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Issuer: Organic Recycling Systems Limited; ISIN INE0MIO01019; BSE543997; BSE SME, not main board. Information cutoff 20 October 2026; market reference 19 October 2026, not the later 21/22 October quotes. The complete FY26 annual report is the latest full-year base, with company updates examined through the cutoff. Share basis is 15,598,905 ordinary shares from the dated security master, independently consistent with the September valuation; lot 900. The investment horizon is 19 October 2026–19 October 2031, using actual 1826 days/365.25 for compounding. Equity hurdle 15% nominal pretax, with 12% and 18% sensitivities;₹500,000 position is illustrative only.
G1 Conditional; G2 Hold — unresolved; G3 Hold — unresolved; G4 Conditional. Confidence is High in quoted audited line items and dated security identity, Medium in the secondary price/turnover evidence, Low in current organic attribution, sustainable incremental returns and available funding. Unmodified audits are positive evidence, not a substitute for missing annexures or economic reconciliation. No existing holding, investor risk profile or allocation recommendation is assumed.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Thirteen primitive factors are evaluated separately: GOV4, MOAT5, REVNS, DUR6, CAPNS, CASH2, BAL3, EXEC5, EARN4, RNS, DNS, PNS, L6. The weighted audit below uses Decimal arithmetic and retains missing factors without assigning neutral values. BQS known contribution 3.24 with 76% weight coverage gives a diagnostic raw range 3.48–5.64, not a score. GQS known contribution 2.00 with 45% coverage gives 2.55–7.50 before the persistent-weak-cash ceiling; final diagnostic upper bound is 5.00 while the point remains NS. IAS has only L's 0.60 contribution and 10% coverage, so its broad diagnostic range 1.50–9.60 is not a ranked value.
IAS Q is the unrounded final BQS, never rounded display or known partial contribution. No governance-failure override is asserted because GOV4 and G1 Conditional do not meet that rule. Missing evidence and G2/G3 exclusion prevent ranking in all three lists. The factor audit records two material facts, contrary evidence, confidence and source references for every factor.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The legacy group develops municipal-solid-waste processing technology, sells engineering/equipment and EPC services, operates the Solapur waste-to-energy platform, and earns consultancy, commission, treatment-product and operating-service income. Domestic projects combine milestone construction cash flows with potential operations and maintenance revenue. Economic performance depends on collection of certified bills, acceptance/testing, feedstock quality and plant uptime, not just waste tonnage or capacity announcements. Public disclosures aggregate unlike activities into one reported business segment, which limits margin attribution.
FY26 revenue categories are products 30.1923 cr, finished goods 8.9619 cr, traded goods 25.1030 cr, services 24.4137 cr, consultancy 11.3159 cr and other commission/minor categories. These labels should not be read as a clean segment bridge. The acquired Industrial Associates business is mainly commodity chemical distribution, with target FY25 revenue 51.90 cr andPAT0.58 cr, not a proprietary high-margin green-chemical producer. Parent FY26 revenue 43.7593 cr and Solapur turnover 36.1947 cr demonstrate a real legacy operation, but standalone and subsidiary totals require intercompany elimination before use as group organic revenue.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
A waste-processing technology reference plant, project credentials and repeated customer awards can lower qualification risk for the next tender and create follow-on O&M work. These are useful competitive mechanisms, not proof of pricing power. The strongest available evidence is operating experience plus specific project wins, rather than a promotional market-size estimate. Engineering competitors, established waste-service operators and alternative biological/thermal technologies can still compete on lifecycle cost and guarantees. Listed waste operators, recycling companies and EPC firms are only imperfect peers; neither their multiples nor margins are imported into this mixed group.
Feedstock heterogeneity, municipal cooperation, site readiness, commissioning performance guarantees and receivable collection can neutralize an apparent technology advantage. Chemical trading brings supplier/customer relationships but little demonstrated durable intellectual-property rent. There is no verified customer-level retention, replacement-cost or market-share series establishing a strong moat. MOAT5 recognizes genuine niche competence with material substitutability; DUR6 recognizes a multiyear project opportunity while withholding a compounder designation.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Reported group revenue moves from 12.5238 cr in FY21 to 14.6137 cr,24.7193 cr,27.4873 cr,48.3906 cr and 105.0746 cr in FY26. The latest increase is 56.6840 cr, or 117.14%. Complete endpoints and CAGR calculations are included, but none is silently labelled latest organic growth. FY25 originalAS operating revenue 43.7729 cr and other income 4.9593 cr become 48.3906 cr and 0.3416 cr under the latest presentation while total income stays 48.7322 cr. That reclassification is not new customer demand.
IA creates a larger uncertainty: January 19 disclosure approves a 14.8293634 cr acquisition with documents targeted within 60 days, whereas annual note 47 consolidates from 12 November 2025. AOC1 reports 59.93 cr IA turnover. Subtracting all 59.93 cr from group 105.0746 cr gives 45.1446 cr, but full-year versus acquisition-period scope and eliminations make that subtraction unsuitable as certified organic growth. Equally, assigning every traded-goods rupee to IA is not proven. Parent revenue and Solapur activity are positive counterevidence against an entirely acquisition-led story. REV remains NS until the exact contribution/price-volume/elimination bridge is published.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The investable runway is the portion of EPC, technology licensing and O&M that can be executed with sufficient working capital and attractive incremental cash returns. The new BPCL awards create demand access; they do not remove milestone retention, performance security or commissioning obligations. A bottom-up path should connect each project to execution period, billing/advance terms, materials/subcontracting, certified collections, performance deposits and aftercare cost. No unsupported conversion of a broad order-value band into annual revenue is used.
The April 24 BOO proposal describes an initial project of roughly 200 cr and five projects totaling 1,000 cr, with about 500 cr company investment over 0–15months. This scale is not funded by 2.8528 cr March cash, the 16.1 cr proposed promoter issue or ordinary reported earnings. It is excluded from the base model, not treated as a committed cash use or free option value. Ongoing development spending is also not free:2.092 cr was capitalized in FY26. Forecast EBITDA margins are after recurring development expense, with separate capital cash costs to avoid counting the same spending twice. Weak cumulative cash conversion triggers the GQS ceiling 5; missingREV/CAP keep the score NS even when the opportunity looks large. A dated October 12 secondary report describes a Bank of Baroda sanction:₹20 cr fund-based and₹10 cr nonfund-based facilities, backed by a parent guarantee. This materially supports financing access, but incremental headroom and draw eligibility are not authenticated; the model separately tests 0/10/20 cr cash draws with interest and repayment.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Capital allocation has combined debt repayment, fresh equity, redemption of legacy preference capital, development assets and acquisitions. The April 2025 filing distinguishes an approved 40,345 preference shares from 21,054 actually redeemed for 26.2076825 cr; only the completed cash flow is used. May 22 redemption is independently documented. Contractual senior redemption is not itself minority abuse, but marketing a net-cash or low-debt story using preference par would badly misdescribe the common-equity economics.
Promoters held 15.07% at August 31; a proposed 1m-share issue at₹161 could increase that to 20.19%, but approval is not a receipt. Low promoter ownership alone is not a governance violation. The May 2025 auditor's complete resignation letter attributes its departure to inability to agree commercially viable fees after completing FY25 audit, and states no other material reason or evidence-access limitation. The FY26 auditor reports no fraud/default and positive audit-trail operation. Historical FY23 CARO uncertainty at two stalled entities is balanced by later FY24/25 clean CARO/actual IFC reports. September executive continuity changes merit monitoring but are not treated as evidence of misconduct. Delivery of projects and cash claims, rather than intentions or association with reputed counterparties, is the execution test.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The main cash warning is persistent: FY23–FY26 PAT totals 52.1239 cr, CFO−12.3047 cr and cash capex 46.0083 cr, giving reportedFCF−58.3130 cr. FY26 alone reports 18.5546 cr CFO, but other-liability movement includes the acquired 14.7323 cr old-partner payable. Removing only that item gives 3.8223 cr, a diagnostic rather than a certified normalization because the acquired asset/cash bridge is incomplete. FY25 accounting restatement is material: originalAS CFO−6.7034 cr and capex 17.2908 cr versus latest IndAS CFO−9.9555 cr and capex 11.2208 cr. Both versions are retained; they are not interchanged opportunistically.
Trade receivables 69.6947 cr plus unbilled 10.0131 cr dominate available cash 2.8528 cr;8.5219 cr of net receivables is over 3 years old. Performance-guarantee term deposits 1.5754 cr are not free cash. Identifiable operating deposits, security liabilities, unbilled assets, capital advances, capital creditors and employee provisions are classified explicitly in the operating-capital bridge. A clean organic incrementalROIC cannot be certified from the computed windows: acquisition scope, AS/IndAS opening profit and PPE depreciation/capitalization differences remain unresolved. CAP is NS, not currentROCE.
Book borrowings 44.9701 cr include 6 cr CCD and preference par, and finance-cost waivers suppress reported interest. Old seller 14.7323 cr, capital creditor 1.2557 cr and current tax 1.0666 cr are handled once; disputed 0.5913 cr is already within capital creditors, not added again. Existing employee claim 1.0645 cr, other short provision 0.1003 cr and old CCD interest 0.0007 cr are retained at terminal. IA ownership 99.99% leaves a tiny minority; the rescue deducts a conservative 0.01% of whole-group enterprise-plus-cash value rather than pretending it is exactly 100%. Pledged operating performance deposits are included in invested capital but excluded from free cash. The service-tax 3.39 cr dispute is a contingent stress, not base debt. A receivable-offset note prints an implausible 588.23 Cr unit; that unit is unresolved, not treated as a new 588 cr claim. Missing FY26 IFC annexures, acquired CFO and depreciation reconciliation driveG2 Hold; immaterial associates and ordinary other-auditor reliance do not by themselves do so.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The authenticated reference price implies₹326.88 cr ordinary market value. Current-share-base FY26 EPS is₹16.08, not the pre-bonus weighted-average EPS printed in the annual report. P/E is 13.03x. Removing other income, applying 25% tax and 8% interest on non CCD/nonpreference debt gives an illustrative PAT₹17.44 cr and P/E18.75x before the separate current-development sensitivity. These are mixed-date diagnostics using the March audited debt/cash balance and August preference count with October price, not certified current net debt. The book EV using preferencepar is misleading: extrapolated actual preference prices alone lift economic-claimEV/EBITDA to about 16.7–16.9x before later accrual and seller settlement.
All ordinary bear/base/bull returns and entry prices are withheld. The dated model tests cash from 31 March 2026, completed May events, seller/old claims,2028 debt and 2029 preference settlement; a lower share price cannot repair issuer funding. A separate explicitly hypothetical retrospective recapitalization fully prefunds every interval before the first reserve breach. It issues even whole pre-bonus shares at a 20% discount to the October reference-price equivalent, charges 2% fees and applies the 1:2bonus without new fractional entitlements. Base gross funding₹261.39 cr produces old-owner dilution 49.99% and conditional five-year return-3.36%; bear-22.49%, bull 20.90%. These are not available funding offers or ordinary target returns.
The funded reverse test at base 24% post-development margin,215working-capital days and 10x exit multiple requires approximately 41.30% annual run-rate growth from FY26 to support 15% equity return, while also resizing the hypothetical issue. Every candidate is fully funded and the bracket/residual is retained. Fixed-rescue-share entry values at 12/15/18% are scenario arithmetic, not recommended buying levels.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not that waste treatment lacks demand. It is that growth consumes cash faster than new common equity can absorb legacy preference claims, seller payments and working capital, while earnings benefit from waived interest, low tax and capitalization. More orders can worsen liquidity before certification and collections. Lower construction margins, slower billing, cash trapped in unbilled assets, premature BOO commitments, redemption accrual and an expensive recapitalization reinforce one another.
A bare book-debt metric would miss the preference economics. Conversely, an assumed 18% accrual on observed redemption prices is not a proven holder-specific liability: the model also tests zero further accrual and different settlement prices/dates. Full 20 cr conditional fund-based draw is stress-tested with interest and repayment under an optimistic group-cash fungibility assumption; sanctioned lines target Solapur BPCL working capital and are not demonstrated parent redemption finance, not treated as 30 cr unrestricted cash or permanent capital. Even strong financing access would not resolve an incorrect acquisition/CFO or ownership bridge. The modeled reserve breaches do not assert that the company was in actual default, and the₹3 cr reserve itself is an analyst assumption. Zero-reserve, seller-settlement, capex, working-capital and contingent-tax tests separate that choice from the much larger funding burden.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A5× or 10× ordinary-equity outcome cannot be inferred from low reported P/E or a large CBG opportunity. At a 10x terminal EBITDA multiple, even a zero-net-cash/zero-senior-claim/no-dilution scale test requires EBITDA equal to half or all of today's market capitalization for 5×/10× equity value. The complete numerical scale tests are retained below. Senior claims and dilution increase the requirement, while a positive terminal cash surplus could reduce it; this is not a universal lower bound.
The bull counterfactual is not a 10-bagger proof: it assumes high growth,29% post-development margin, faster working-capital realization, no further preference accrual and a 13x terminal multiple, plus a large fully prefunded recapitalization. Ordinary financing is unverified and the base case does not approach the return hurdle. Treat 5×/10× as a high-bar falsifiable operating-and-financing exercise, not a price target. A credible route would need cash-generative project execution, much larger sustainable earnings and a capital structure that preserves per-share participation.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Obtain holder-level preference shares, original issue prices, accrual dates and binding March 2029 redemption schedule; reconcile 108,549 remaining shares to each settlement.
2. Reconcile FY26 acquired IA balances, effective control date, post-acquisition revenue/PAT and CFO; confirm old-partner 14.7323 cr payment date and source.
3. Obtain actual FY26 IFC annexures and the 465.44-versus 249.57 lakhs depreciation bridge; a signed explanation is more useful than a clean main opinion alone.
4. Track net receivables 69.6947 cr, unbilled 10.0131 cr and over 3year 8.5219 cr. Further aging without receipts is a warning even if revenue grows.
5. Reconcile current cash, restricted deposits, bank utilization and eligible undrawn funds; distinguish 20 cr fund limits from 10 cr nonfund exposure and avoid double-counting replacement facilities.
6. Verify whether 1m promoter shares at₹161 are allotted and cash received; update the share count and actual use of proceeds, not just approvals.
7. Track project commissioning, certification, cash advances, performance/security claims and O&M economics; obtain backlog without duplicate or aspirational entries.
8. Separate recurring R&D expense from purchased assets and construction spending; monitor FCF and cash tax as losses/waivers expire.
9. Require financing before any 500 cr BOO deployment; a materially unfinanced contractual commitment would changeG3, while a vague proposal alone is not a current default.
10. Before any trade, verify BSE restrictions,900 lot and executable spread/depth. This is a research checklist, not an automated monitoring arrangement.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold — unresolved; refinancing-dependent project-growth special situation with meaningful operating capability and weak verified cash realization. Research priority is the capital-claim and acquisition reconciliation, not waiting for a mechanically lower quote. It is not an evidence-backed compounder candidate because REV/CAP are unscored, CASH/BAL are weak and critical gates remain unresolved. There is no justified governance-failure or presently distressed/default label solely from the retrieved evidence.
No BQS, GQS or IAS rank is assigned. A future eligible setup would require a reliable comparable earnings/capital/cash bridge, binding funding through the preference maturity and project execution period, a precise subsidiary CCD/ordinary-share ownership calculation, and acceptable whole-lot tradability. A funded counterfactual can inform how expensive recapitalization might be, but cannot turn absent financing into a current investment case. Once those conditions are met, rerun both price-dependent returns and downside tests rather than carrying forward this date's conditional numbers. This report does not instruct a purchase, sale or portfolio allocation.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The linked source ledger distinguishes original company/exchange documents from dated secondary market or announcement evidence. Full primary annual reports, notes and auditor material for FY23–FY26, IPO restated FY21–FY23 accounts, acquisition, preference, bonus and proposed issue filings were examined. Source hashes authenticate the retained payload used for this analysis; they do not make an inaccessible original document independently available. Archived extracts preserve only needed financial facts and calculation inputs, not whole source reports or shareholder identifiers.
Important unresolved items are the actual FY26 IFC annexures; acquisition timing, eliminations and cash-flow classification; the PPE/development depreciation bridge; holder-specific preference terms; subsidiary CCD issuer and ownership effect; and incremental eligible current funding. The May 15 redemption is a dated secondary/count-reconciliation observation with a located but inaccessible primary link. Current facilities and latest order updates retain their secondary qualification where original PDFs were unavailable. Quarterly interpolation, normalization tax/interest, cash reserve, settlement timing, recapitalization pricing and terminal multiples are analyst assumptions, not management guidance.
Cash models stop at 19 October 2031 and preserve terminal operating reserve and known claims. No post-terminal borrowing is included, no noncash swap is treated as cash, and no optional equity receipt is silently assumed. Historical/model/sensitivity rows are embedded completely in the canonical record and reproducible from the accompanying financial extracts and builders.

evidence.claim: FY26 group revenue105.0746cr/PAT25.0806cr versus restatedFY25 revenue48.3906cr/PAT15.6205cr.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: AnnualFY25 originally classified4.6177cr more income outside operating revenue; FY26 includes newly acquired Industrial Associates.

evidence.claim: IA consideration14.8293634cr for99.99%; targetFY25 revenue51.90cr/PAT0.58cr. Annualnote47 uses12Nov2025 consolidation but January19 approval says acquisition approved that day.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: AOC1 FY26 turnover59.93cr is not a verified acquisition-period contribution after group eliminations. Subtracting it from105.0746cr is only diagnostic.

evidence.claim: FY26 CFO18.5546cr includes14.6368cr increase in other liabilities; closing other current liabilities include14.7323cr IA old-partner liability.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Subtracting the seller liability gives3.8223cr diagnostic CFO but does not reconcile acquired assets, acquisition cash or consolidation dates.

evidence.claim: FY23–FY26 cumulative reported CFO−12.3047cr versus PAT52.1239cr, with46.0083cr cash capex and−58.3130cr cumulative FCF.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Mixed AS/IndAS comparability is explicit; FY26 positive cashflow is real reported evidence but not enough to erase persistent poor realization.

evidence.claim: Remaining preference count108,549 at August31; actualMay22 prices₹12,500 and₹13,175. Applying those prices gives135.68625–143.0133075cr before later accrual, compared with0.108549cr par.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: This is a transparent liability sensitivity, not a certified holder-specific redemption amount. Agreements and price clocks remain incomplete.

evidence.claim: FY26 preference redemption21,054 shares cost26.2076825cr; May22 another11,649 cost15.151065cr. Both use fresh equity proceeds.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: May15 redemption16,380/20.475cr is secondary and count-reconciled, not an obtained primary PDF. May warrant proceeds are nearly matched by redemptions, not all spare growth cash.

evidence.claim: FY26 main audit opinions are unmodified, and audit-trail reporting is positive; no current lender default or fraud was reported in inspected standalone CARO.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Actual FY26 standalone IFC AnnexureB was not located; consolidated report points to Note40, which describes consolidation scope, not a full IFC annexure.

evidence.claim: Two unaudited associates have only0.0052cr aggregate recorded investment exposure and are inactive/small; other-auditor subsidiaries account for150.56cr assets and61.83cr revenue.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Ordinary other-auditor reliance and immaterial associates are not themselves misconduct or the sole basis of G2 Hold.

evidence.claim: FY23 consolidated CARO noted uncertainty at two loss-making entities; FY24/25 report no adverse CARO findings and contain actual unmodified IFC annexures. May2025 auditor resigned over fee viability after completingFY25 audit.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Historical issues are not assumed current defaults; resignation letter expressly identifies no other material reason or management evidence limitation.

evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Capitalization or scope may explain differences; no verified bridge was obtained. Do not call these figures fraudulent or definitively misstated.

evidence.claim: Net trade receivables69.6947cr, unbilled10.0131cr, including8.5219cr of receivables over3years; FY26 operating reserve cash only2.8528cr, while1.5754cr term deposits are pledged performance guarantees.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Payment terms60–180days and project milestones explain some working-capital intensity, but do not authenticate collection of aged balances.

evidence.claim: FY26 book borrowings44.9701cr include6cr CCD and0.1366cr preference par; lease liabilities0.7731cr; reported ICD34.4273cr has mixed on/before and on/afterMarch2028 wording.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Low current financecost depends on waivers; CCD issuer/conversion attribution and mapped external maturity schedule need confirmation. Parent intercompany lending is not added twice.

evidence.claim: Physical/development investment and working-capital capital rise materially; diagnosticFY24–26 incremental operating returns are not a clean organic return series.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: IndAS transition, acquired business and capitalized-depreciation differences prevent a defensible CAP score. Current ROCE is not substituted.

evidence.claim: BOO proposal contemplates five projects totaling1,000cr and roughly500cr company investment over0–15months; September proposal adds1m promoter shares at₹161, gross16.1cr.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Neither proposal is treated as received or committed funding in actual cash. Large announced markets or signed orders are not cash receipts.

evidence.claim: Solapur operating assets, technology development, EPC contracts and later O&M provide a real operating franchise; January/February and September BPCL contract disclosures support demand access.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Bid competition, heterogeneous feedstock, testing guarantees, municipal collections and low-margin chemical distribution limit moat and cash durability.

evidence.claim: ₹209.55 close on19October is retained in dated secondary history and corroborated IIFL; all60 calendar sessions have valid OHLC/volume observations,45 have actual trade value.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: For15 sessions, restored prebonus low×rawvolume is a conservative trade-value bound, not actual VWAP turnover. Raw NSE files contain no issuer row; they are not zero-volume observations.

evidence.claim: ₹500,000 illustrative position is below3 lots:2 lots1800shares cost₹377,190;3lots2700shares cost₹565,785. Conservative20/60session median value supports underone fractional day at5% participation.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: A large lot makes sizing coarse. Snapshot spread, surveillance, concentration and queue liquidity are incompletely authenticated.

evidence.claim: FY26 current development capitalization2.092cr, compared with2.358cr FY25, raises EBITDA relative to expensing the same cash outlays.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Research may create real reusable technology; current-development expensing is a sensitivity, not a full retrospective accounting restatement.

evidence.claim: Promoter holding15.07% atAugust31 and proposed postissue20.19%; low holding alone is not a governance failure.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Repeated equity financing, preference priorities and possible subsidiary CCD dilution need a common-equity ownership bridge.

evidence.claim: Standalone₹43.7593cr revenue and Solapur₹36.1947cr turnover show legacy operations are meaningful rather than a pure acquired trading shell.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Adding subsidiaries without eliminating internal transactions or removing acquisition-period effects cannot certify current organic growth.

evidence.claim: The current model has positive counterfactual economics only under large, wholly hypothetical prefunding; ordinary and nonrescue returns stay unscored after cash-floor breaches.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: The₹3cr reserve is analyst-selected, not evidence of insolvency. Zero-reserve and funding sensitivities still show substantial modeled gaps.

summary: Hold — unresolved. Organic Recycling Systems is a municipal-waste technology, EPC and waste-to-energy operating group, now also exposed to acquired chemical distribution. It is a project-growth and refinancing special situation, not an established compounder. Repeat projects and the Solapur operating franchise are the strongest evidence for the business; poor cumulative cash realization, an unbridged acquisition and economically large preference claims are the decisive risks. At the qualified 19 October price₹209.55, market capitalization is₹326.88 cr and reported FY26 P/E is 13.03x. That optical multiple ignores the difference between preference par and actual redemption economics. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS rather than imputed scores. No ordinary entry range is supported. Obtain a reliable acquisition/cash/claim bridge and binding funded execution plan before considering price as the main obstacle.
